correctness.rationale: The radial derivative on each prescribed circle is zero and the angular speed is a+b cos θ with a>|b| and a²−b²=ω². One turn is therefore exactly one least physical period. Linearization of dr/dθ has numerator 2Kr_iF′(s_i)cos θ and no angular-denominator derivative term because F(s_i)=0. The quotient's cosine integral is −T_i w_i, giving the exact log multiplier. Choosing K above the finite maximum puts all w_i in (−1,1); the two degree-(m−1) interpolants impose their values independently. The x-component on y=0 proves degree 2m, including m=1. For the lower bound, division in y by y²+x²−s_i and evaluation on the two open semicircles gives zero remainder. The relatively prime factors together divide xP+yQ. At degree below 2m the quotient is constant, and the origin forces it to vanish. In that case radius is a first integral and regularity of a designated orbit gives an annulus of regular periodic circles, excluding hyperbolicity. Independent Cartesian ODE integration and divergence accumulation reproduced periods 2, 3.7, 1.5 and multipliers 0.66, 0.85, 1.55 on three radii, including two adjacent attracting circles. Replay: python3 branches/independent_checks.py 5 (NumPy/SciPy).
residual_risks: The bounded numerical evidence tests one nonuniform period/stability profile only; the algebraic and variational argument proves arbitrary data. Other periodic orbits and incomplete global flows are allowed.
